item.text:
**4B.7 Research Note**

Overall judgment: **No**. I found a few public statements and institutional moves that gesture toward inclusion, but the 2024 record is much stronger on exclusion, discriminatory enforcement, and repression of minorities, Baloch activists, and opposition voices.

- [PM reassures equal opportunities for minorities](https://www.radio.gov.pk/11-08-2024/pm-reassures-equal-opportunities-for-minorities) - **Radio Pakistan**, 2024-08-11. Claim: On National Minority Day, Sharif said minorities play a significant role in Pakistan’s stability and prosperity, that their rights are constitutionally guaranteed, and that the government would protect minority rights and equal opportunity. This is the clearest positive statement for political equality, though it is rhetorical rather than proof of durable policy change. **QIDs:** 4B.7, 4B.5.

- [Government acknowledges human-rights bodies and inclusive protections](https://pid.gov.pk/site/press_detail/27376) - **Press Information Department, Pakistan**, 2024-12-10. Claim: The government said it had enacted legislative measures for vulnerable groups, noted autonomous commissions for women, children, and human rights, and said the National Commission for Minorities had strengthened minority-rights protection. This is a formal-institution positive, but it does not show that Sharif successfully protected equality when politically costly. **QIDs:** 4B.7, 4B.4.

- [Pakistan: Amnesty International condemns harassment faced by Baloch protestors in Islamabad](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/01/pakistan-amnesty-international-condemns-harassment-faced-by-baloch-protestors-in-islamabad/) - **Amnesty International**, 2024-01-24. Claim: Amnesty said Baloch women and families protesting enforced disappearances were harassed, intimidated, arbitrarily arrested, and subjected to disinformation while exercising peaceful assembly. This is strong evidence against protecting an excluded group’s equal political standing. **QIDs:** 4B.7, 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.8, 3B.9.

- [Pakistan: Repeated punitive crackdowns on Baloch protests must end](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/pakistan-repeated-punitive-crackdowns-on-baloch-protests-must-end/) - **Amnesty International**, 2024-07-30. Claim: Amnesty described deaths, mass arrests, roadblocks, and network shutdowns against Baloch protesters, saying authorities were punishing peaceful political mobilization rather than protecting equal citizenship. This is among the strongest negative items for opposition regions and excluded groups. **QIDs:** 4B.7, 4B.3, 4B.2, 3B.8, 3B.9, 3B.10.

- [Pakistan: Widening Crackdown on Dissent](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/pakistan-widening-crackdown-dissent) - **Human Rights Watch**, 2024-01-11. Claim: HRW said the government clamped down on dissenting media, the opposition, and NGOs, and that undocumented Afghans and other vulnerable people faced abuse and weak safeguards. This shows broad hostility to unpopular viewpoints and vulnerable groups rather than equal political protection. **QIDs:** 4B.7, 4B.6, 4B.5, 4B.4, 4B.3.

- [World Report 2024: Pakistan](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/pakistan) - **Human Rights Watch**, 2024. Claim: HRW reported that transgender women remained under attack and that the government did little to stop early and forced marriage, while women and minority communities remained vulnerable to discrimination and abuse. This undercuts any claim of strong protection for women and gender minorities. **QIDs:** 4B.7, 3B.7, 3B.4.

- [Pakistan report](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128431.html) - **U.S. Department of State**, 2024. Claim: The report says authorities used PEMRA, network access, and government advertising to suppress threatening media, and officials pushed journalists toward a predetermined narrative. That is evidence against equal political treatment for unpopular viewpoints and excluded voices. **QIDs:** 4B.7, 4B.6, 4B.5, 4B.4, 4B.3.

- [Pakistan: The new Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act threatens the right to protest](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/pakistan-the-new-peaceful-assembly-and-public-order-act-threatens-the-right-to-protest/) - **Amnesty International**, 2024-09-09. Claim: Amnesty said the new law criminalized peaceful assembly and expanded state power to restrict gatherings, reinforcing unequal treatment of political outsiders and protest movements. **QIDs:** 4B.7, 4B.6, 4B.5, 4B.4, 4B.3, 4B.2.

- [Pakistan: The election-day internet shutdown was a reckless attack on people’s rights](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/pakistan-election-day-internet-shutdown-is-a-reckless-attack-on-peoples-rights/) - **Amnesty International**, 2024-02-08. Claim: The election-day telecom and mobile internet shutdown hit everyone, but it disproportionately impaired opposition mobilization, civil-society monitoring, and access for excluded groups. This is negative evidence against equal political access. **QIDs:** 4B.7, 4B.6, 4B.5, 4B.3, 4B.2.

- [Pakistan election environment concerns](https://www.theprint.in/world/us-uk-eu-urge-probe-into-pakistan-election-express-concerns/1961577/) - **Reuters**, 2024-02-10. Claim: External partners raised concerns about interference, irregularities, and fraud, which supports the view that political equality in the election environment was not being protected. **QIDs:** 4B.7, 4B.1, 4B.2.

**Search gap**

- I found **limited positive evidence** for minorities and inclusive institutions, mainly official rhetoric and commission-level structures.
- I found **no strong 2024 evidence** that Sharif protected minorities, women, Baloch citizens, transgender people, or opposition regions when doing so would have required confronting security forces, party allies, or entrenched state practices.
- The balance of evidence points to **unequal protection and selective coercion**, not political equality.
